newsitem.title: USA: FORECAST - U.S. crude runs seen staying high.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - U.S. crude runs seen staying high.

text.p: REUTER SURVEY ESTIMATES* ACTUAL STOCKS FOR
FOR WEEK ENDED 06/06/97 WEEK ENDED 05/30/97-CHANGE
DISTILLATE......UP 2.50 million bbls 102.228 UP 5.087 MLN
GASOLINE........UP 1.12 million bbls 199.723 DN 2.945 MLN
UTILIZATION... DN 0.25 98.4 DN 1.7 PCT
*NB - The survey estimate is derived by omitting the high and low forecast and averaging the rest, with a sample of at least six.
(STOCKS IN THOUSANDS/BBLS, CHANGES IN MLN/BBLS)
Refinery runs are expected to remain at or near record levels in Tuesday's American Petroleum Institute weekly status report, according to analysts surveyed by Reuters.

The runs rate is expected to be unchanged or only slightly down from the previous week, when refineries in the districts east of the Rocky Mountains (PADDs I-IV) were running at 99.9 percent. The rate in the country as a whole was 98.4 percent.
Analysts also were in broad agreement that distillates stocks would continue to rise, with almost all six of those surveyed looking for a build of 2.5 million barrels in the week ended June 6.

But there was a wide range of forecasts for crude oil inventories, reflecting a fair degree of skepticism about the recent rise in stocks, which occured even while the refinery runs rate was climbing sharply.
Also, there were different views of what gasoline stocks did last week, though the balance was in favor of build of more than a million barrels.

"These runs are gradually translating into very high heating oil stocks. By next Tuesday stocks will be the second highest in 12 years, possibly the highest," said Jim Ritterbusch at Sweeney Oil in Chicago.
"Once heating oil joins in (the selloff), you'll see refining runs cut. The heat crack will lose a buck," Ritterbush predicts.
On gasoline, analysts either see the record production level of nearly 8.2 million barrels per day continuing or a slight slowdown.

"Output can't stay at the levels we saw last week and I figure imports will be down and with the holiday weekend (Memorial Day Monday of last week), we'll see a draw of between 1.5 and 2.5 million," said Tom Bentz of High Yield Analytics in New York.
Those looking for a draw on crude point to the high level of runs together with high imports and expect a correction in the statistics that have also been recording rising inventory levels.
But some looking for another rise think a draw in stocks will have to wait until imports are choked off.
"The arbitrage from Europe is not shut tight but that won't show up until next week's numbers," said an analyst at Prudential Securities in New York.
--Tony McAuley, New York Energy Desk, +1 212 859 1623
